cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3). He opens by telling the LORD he'll sing of His loving devotion and His justice. Then David starts making promises, friend, and I mean promise after promise after PROMISE.
David says he'll ponder the way that is blameless. Then, right in the middle of that thought, he asks the LORD, "when will You come to me?"
Then David makes a big promise: he will walk with integrity of heart. And he names exactly where he's going to do it.

cards.question: Where does David say he'll walk with integrity of heart?

cards.text: Next, David makes a promise about his eyes: he'll set no worthless thing before them. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer staring at a takeout menu for a restaurant that closed, so I respect this man deeply.

cards.question: Then David talks about the work of those who fall away. What does he say about it?

answers.text: He hates it and it won't cling to him
He'll study it so he can learn from it
He'll leave it for someone else to judge

cards.text: Then David says a perverse heart shall depart from him. Not step out for a minute, not be right back, just DEPART.

cards.question: Along with a perverse heart departing, David says he will know nothing of ___.

cards.text: Now David turns to the people around him, and some of them are about to have a VERY awkward meeting.

cards.question: What does David say he'll do to whoever slanders a neighbor in secret?
David says the one with haughty eyes and a proud heart is someone he will not endure. True or false?

cards.text: But David isn't only showing people the door. His eyes are out looking for someone, like a boss scrolling résumés with a VERY short list of what he's hiring for.

cards.question: Who do David's eyes favor, so they may dwell with him?

answers.text: The wise men of the east

cards.question: And the person who walks in the way of integrity? David says they'll get to ___ to him.

cards.text: Then David gets to two kinds of people in the same verse: the ones who practice deceit and the ones who tell lies. Somebody's about to find out where they stand.

cards.question: David says someone who practices deceit can still dwell in his house. True or false?

cards.text: And David isn't saving this for someday. He puts it on a schedule, like the friend who makes a workout plan and then ACTUALLY sticks to it.

cards.question: When does David say he'll remove all the wicked of the land?
Early on, David promised to walk with integrity in his own house. In the last line, his clean-up stays inside his house and goes no farther. True or false?
